problem: Express $2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{3\pi }{7})\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{3\pi }{7})$ as a single trigonometric ratio.
worked_solution:
First, let's recall the double-angle formula for sine: 

$$
2\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡x=\operatorname{sin}⁡2x
$$

Substituting $x=\frac{3\pi }{7}$ into the above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{3\pi }{7})\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{3\pi }{7}) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\cdot \frac{3\pi }{7})=\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{6\pi }{7}).\end{aligned}
$$
